fuente.nota: Text shortened by paragraphs; sentences unchanged.

parrafos: As pollution grows, ways to combat it have been in demand. Solar energy and wind energy give people clean opportunities to power their homes. But these may also have environmental issues depending on the situation. When people use these alternative forms of energy, they put less carbon dioxide into the environment.

Water pollution is the presence of harmful materials in water, such as sewage, dissolved metal, waste from farms, factories and crude oil spilled from oil tankers. The three main substances that pollute water are nitrates from fertilizers, sewage, and detergents.

Activities such as bathing and washing clothes near lakes, ponds or rivers add nutrients like nitrate and phosphate into the water bodies.This leads to excessive growth of algae on the surface of water. It blocks the penetration of sunlight and air, thus reducing oxygen.
It causes harm to organisms living in water and can also harm people's health. In extreme cases, it may cause diseases like cancer. It also leads to loss of a large amount of aquatic life.

Water pollution has been a problem from the time human population increased, and live in cities. Cities have been prone to cholera and typhoid fever and other infectious diseases since Roman times. Existing water systems put in place in the 19th century are overwhelmed by the rapid growth of population in cities.

Air can be polluted by many things. Examples include poisonous gases, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide and very small particulates. Smoke and harmful gases released by fires, industries, and thermal power plants cause air pollution. Using coal and wood as fuels for fire causes a lot of air pollution. Petroleum produces less pollution per ton, but it causes a lot of pollution since a lot of it is burned globally. Air pollution may cause health problems such as asthma or other breathing problems.

Noise pollution, also known as sound pollution, is harmful to the brain and hearing of all animals and humans. This includes the sound of vehicles, loud speakers, airplanes, jets, train horns etc. Noise pollution can cause ear problems or even permanent deafness, especially to older people. The schools which are beside the roads suffer from the car exhaust fumes as well as noise pollution caused by cars. Students cannot concentrate in their studies sometimes because of noise pollution. People in hospitals near main roads also suffer.
Thermal pollution is the harmful release of heated liquid into a body of water or heat released into the air as a waste product of an industry.

A common cause of thermal pollution is using water as a coolant by power stations and industrial manufacturers. This puts back warm water, and so raises the temperature and decreases how much oxygen is in the water. The heat released into the air will make the air warmer which increase global warming.
resumen_es: Presents clean energy as a response to pollution and describes four types: water, air, noise and thermal pollution, with their causes and effects on health and the environment.

ideas_clave.idea: Clean energy sources such as solar and wind power help to reduce carbon dioxide emissions, although they are not entirely free of environmental problems.
Water is polluted mainly by fertilisers, sewage and detergents, whose nutrients cause algae to spread, cutting off light and oxygen and harming aquatic life and human health.
Urbanisation has long exposed cities to waterborne diseases, and nineteenth-century water systems cannot cope with today's population growth.
Air pollution, caused by toxic gases and particles from fires, industry, power plants and fossil fuels, can lead to respiratory illnesses.
Noise from traffic, aircraft and loudspeakers damages hearing and makes it hard for pupils and patients near busy roads to concentrate or rest.
Thermal pollution occurs when industries and power stations release heated water or air, reducing oxygen in rivers and adding to global warming.

resumen_modelo: The text examines the main forms of pollution and some ways of tackling it. It first points out that solar and wind power reduce carbon dioxide emissions, even though they may raise environmental issues of their own. Water pollution, mostly caused by fertilisers, sewage and detergents, encourages the excessive growth of algae, which deprives water of light and oxygen, endangering aquatic life and human health; moreover, ageing urban water systems struggle to cope with population growth. Air pollution, produced by fires, industry and the burning of fuels, causes breathing problems, while noise damages hearing and disturbs schools and hospitals. Finally, thermal pollution, mainly from power stations using water as a coolant, reduces oxygen in water and contributes to global warming.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, solar and wind energy never cause any environmental problems.
preguntas.cita: But these may also have environmental issues depending on the situation.
preguntas.explicacion: The text adds that they can also cause environmental problems depending on the situation, even though they emit less CO2.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following is NOT listed among the three main substances that pollute water?
preguntas.cita: The three main substances that pollute water are nitrates from fertilizers, sewage, and detergents.
preguntas.explicacion: Crude oil is mentioned as a water pollutant, but not among the three main substances, which are nitrates, sewage and detergents.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 1 a word meaning “dirty water and waste carried away from homes” (es: aguas residuales).
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning waste water from toilets and drains.
preguntas.cita: such as sewage, dissolved metal, waste from farms, factories and crude oil
preguntas.explicacion: “Sewage” is waste water (es: aguas residuales); a “sewer” is the underground pipe that carries it (es: alcantarilla).

preguntas.enunciado: Answer in your own words (1–3 sentences).
preguntas.pregunta: Explain how washing clothes near a lake can reduce the oxygen in its water.
respuestas: Washing adds nutrients such as nitrate and phosphate to the water, which makes algae grow excessively on the surface; the algae block sunlight and air, so the oxygen in the water falls.
preguntas.cita: This leads to excessive growth of algae on the surface of water. It blocks the penetration of sunlight and air, thus reducing oxygen.
preguntas.explicacion: It is a chain of causes: nutrients, algal growth, light and air blocked, less oxygen (eutrophication).

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: In extreme cases, water pollution may cause diseases like cancer.
preguntas.cita: In extreme cases, it may cause diseases like cancer.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so for extreme cases, as well as the harm to aquatic organisms.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are water systems built in the 19th century now overwhelmed?
opciones: Because of the rapid growth of urban populations
Because they were badly designed by the Romans
Because of thermal pollution from power stations
Because of the increase in noise pollution
respuestas: Because of the rapid growth of urban populations
preguntas.cita: Existing water systems put in place in the 19th century are overwhelmed by the rapid growth of population in cities.
preguntas.explicacion: The cause is the rapid growth of the urban population. The Romans are mentioned only as a time reference for the epidemics.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 4 an expression meaning “likely to suffer from, exposed to” (es: propensas a, expuestas a).
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'likely to suffer from'.
preguntas.cita: Cities have been prone to cholera and typhoid fever and other infectious diseases since Roman times.
preguntas.explicacion: “Prone to” means likely to suffer from something; it is used mainly with negative things (prone to accidents, prone to flooding).

preguntas.pregunta: Why does petroleum cause a lot of air pollution, according to the text?
opciones: Because a large amount of it is burned around the world
Because it produces more pollution per ton than coal
Because it releases heated water into rivers
Because it is mainly used by thermal power plants
respuestas: Because a large amount of it is burned around the world
preguntas.cita: Petroleum produces less pollution per ton, but it causes a lot of pollution since a lot of it is burned globally.
preguntas.explicacion: It pollutes less per tonne, but it is burnt in large quantities. The second option says the opposite of the text and the others are not mentioned.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Air pollution is the main cause of death in large cities.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says that air pollution can cause asthma or other breathing problems, but it does not talk about deaths.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Noise pollution can cause permanent deafness, especially among young people.
preguntas.cita: Noise pollution can cause ear problems or even permanent deafness, especially to older people.
preguntas.explicacion: The text points to older people as especially affected, not young people.

preguntas.enunciado: Answer in your own words (1–3 sentences).
preguntas.pregunta: Why are schools located next to main roads particularly affected by pollution?
respuestas: Because they suffer both from exhaust fumes and from traffic noise, which sometimes prevents students from concentrating on their studies.
preguntas.cita: The schools which are beside the roads suffer from the car exhaust fumes as well as noise pollution caused by cars.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer should cover the two types of pollution (fumes and noise) and their effect on concentration.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 8 a word meaning “a liquid used to cool machines” (es: refrigerante).
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning a substance used to cool machines.
preguntas.cita: A common cause of thermal pollution is using water as a coolant by power stations and industrial manufacturers.
preguntas.explicacion: “Coolant” is a liquid used for cooling (es: refrigerante); power stations use water to cool down and return it hot.

tribunal.pista_es: Explain the mechanism of nitrates and algae.

tribunal.pista_es: Link with Spain: Mar Menor, urban air quality, nitrates.
ideas: air quality in Madrid and Barcelona and low-emission zones

tribunal.pregunta: From an economic point of view, why does pollution occur, and how can it be corrected?
tribunal.pista_es: Negative externalities: Pigouvian taxes, emission allowances, regulation.

tribunal.pregunta: Is the EU Emissions Trading System an effective tool to reduce pollution?
tribunal.pista_es: Assessment of the EU ETS and its reform.

tribunal.pregunta: Should the EU impose a carbon tax on imports from countries with weaker environmental rules?
tribunal.pista_es: Trade policy: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), carbon leakage, WTO.

tribunal.pregunta: In your opinion, can economic growth be compatible with environmental protection?
tribunal.pista_es: Demanding opinion: decoupling, green growth, degrowth.
